I spent a lot of money, too, buying all these supplies for my projects and new clothes, even though I didn't really have the funds. I was talking really fast, interrupting people, and I just felt so incredibly important and brilliant. I even started picking up women at bars, which is way out of character for me. It lasted for about a week before everything crashed back down to this gray numbness again. That was a really distinct change from how I usually am, and it caused some real problems.

It’s been, gosh, over three years now, this heavy cloud just follows me. Every day feels like trudging through mud. I’m constantly sad, just a low hum of gloom that never really lifts. It’s impossible to focus on my art, let alone my studies; my mind just drifts, and I can't concentrate on anything, whether it's a critique or just trying to read. I used to be so confident in my work, but now I second-guess every stroke, every idea, feeling totally incapable.

But the thing is, sometimes it's like a switch flips. For a few weeks a year or so ago, it was the complete opposite. I was buzzing with energy, barely sleeping, filled with these incredible, grandiose ideas for my installations. I felt brilliant, on top of the world, sketching and creating non-stop for days. I actually finished a whole collection in a week, something that usually takes months. It felt amazing at the time, but looking back, I can see it wasn't quite… normal. My friends said I was talking a mile a minute, jumping from one thing to the next, and my art got really abstract and almost frenetic. It eventually crashed, of course, and then the familiar grey returned.
